Some questions are actively disputed between research groups. One lab's report of unusual microclots in long COVID blood has been directly challenged by another group using different measurement methods, and studies of autoantibodies against cell-surface receptors have produced conflicting results depending on which assay was used. Other questions haven't been adequately studied at all: why the same infection leaves one person fully recovered and another chronically ill, whether one mechanism or several different ones produce the same symptom cluster in different people, and which findings from long COVID research actually transfer to ME/CFS, post-treatment Lyme disease, or post-Ebola syndrome. That cross-condition testing is only just beginning.
